The long-word splitting and empty-input handling look right. The problem is the change from `<=` to `<`, which the PR says was added only so `test_meeting_reminder` passes.

- It contradicts the docstring, which says lines can be "at most `width`" characters. Lines built from two or more words now stop at `width - 1`.
- It's inconsistent: a single word or split chunk can still be exactly `width` long, but joined words can't reach it. The real limit depends on how the line was built, so this isn't a coherent rule.
- The code now follows whatever this one test expects instead of a clear spec, and other callers relying on the documented behaviour will quietly get shorter lines.

The test and the docstring disagree, so a person needs to decide which is right. Check with the teammate or the notifications team whether width is meant to be exclusive:
- If it is: update the docstring to say so, and apply the rule the same way everywhere, including splitting long words into chunks of `width - 1`.
- If it isn't: the test's expected value is wrong. Raise that with the teammate rather than changing the code to match it.

Please drop the `<` change, or make it consistent with an updated docstring once that decision is made. The PR description should also put this conflict up front.
